items.headline: Santa Clara agenda lists $3.8M power-modeling software deal for Silicon Valley Power
items.summary: The November 10 City Council agenda listed an action to let the City Manager sign an agreement with cQuant.io, Inc. for generation resource modeling software for Silicon Valley Power, the city-owned electric utility. The maximum compensation was $3,791,855 over a ten-year term.

items.headline: Planning Commission agenda: 251-unit Eden Housing project on N. Wolfe Road
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed Architectural and Site Approval and Tree Removal Permits for a 251-unit residential development by Eden Housing at 10333 N. Wolfe Road. The proposal includes site and trail improvements and the removal and replacement of 117 protected trees.

items.headline: Planning Commission agenda: 363 apartments proposed on Stevens Creek Boulevard office site
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed a proposal by The Hanover Company for a 363-unit apartment development at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, replacing existing office buildings. The site is on Sites 5 and 6 of the city's Priority Housing Sites in the 6th Cycle Housing Element, and the project uses SB 330 and State Density Bonus law.

items.headline: Preschool for up to 192 kids proposed at 855 E. Homestead
items.summary: The Planning Commission's November 9 agenda listed a Special Development Permit to demolish a vacant commercial building at 855 E. Homestead Road and build a 16,000-square-foot, two-story Primrose childcare and preschool for up to 192 children. The plan includes a new eight-foot masonry wall along the western and part of the southern property lines.

items.headline: Historic Commission agenda: 1,200 sq ft backyard unit at 1391 Washington Street
items.summary: The Historical and Landmarks Commission's November 5 agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street, a property on the Historic Resource Inventory (PLN26-00020). The same agenda also listed choosing one commissioner to sit on the review board that selects a consultant for the city's Historic Preservation Ordinance update.

items.headline: Heritage commission agenda: history update on Asian American contributions and SB 9 changes
items.summary: The November 4 Heritage Preservation Commission agenda listed a draft update to the city's Historical Context Statement to include contributions by Asian Americans and other minority groups. It also listed a presentation on recent changes to SB 9 (including SB 450 and AB 1061) affecting two-unit developments and urban lot splits in single-family zones.

items.headline: Campbell Technology Park housing plan includes pedestrian crossing upgrades
items.summary: Staff said the project adds a net 1,368 daily trips. Required transportation measures include a mid-block crosswalk on Campbell Technology Parkway and another at East McGlincy Lane. A separate city restriping of Camden/White Oaks, where about 30 vehicles already queue, is not a condition of approval. The developer agreed to record easements for a possible future bike/pedestrian bridge over Highway 17, but a feasibility-study grant application failed.

items.headline: White Oaks Manor neighbors protest 14 townhomes planned for three single-family lots
items.summary: At the November 2 oral requests, residents of the White Oaks Manor neighborhood, some holding yard signs, objected to 14 townhomes replacing three single-family homes. They also asked about the city's housing element number and voiced support for a demolition control ordinance. One speaker said they watched an October 27 Planning Commission meeting where developers opposed that ordinance.
